events.asset: MAPS ibogaine research programme for substance use disorders: funding
events.title: MAPS ibogaine research for substance use disorders is fully funded
events.proposition: MAPS announces that its ibogaine research programme for substance use disorders is fully funded, by public money or by donors, through to an FDA decision.
events.criterion: TRUE on the date of a definitive public announcement by MAPS (press release, annual report or MAPS Bulletin), or by the entity that runs the MAPS ibogaine research programme for substance use disorders, that the programme is fully funded by government money or by donations for the work needed to reach an FDA decision. A single grant, a donation, a fundraising target or a pledge that MAPS does not state covers the whole programme does not count, and funding raised by a for-profit sponsor as equity does not count. FALSE at the deadline when no such announcement exists. Resolution source: MAPS press releases and the MAPS Bulletin.

resolution_source.name: MAPS press releases and MAPS Bulletin

readings: 'If we can get the research on ibogaine for substance use disorders fully funded with public money or by donors' is the event: MAPS states the programme is fully funded.
'Public money or by donors' is 'or', so either funding route counts; the amount is not named, so MAPS's own statement that the programme is fully funded settles it.
'Fully funded' is read as funded through to an FDA decision, the horizon named in the same sentence.

related_timeline.event: Colorado voters approve Proposition 122 (Natural Medicine Health Act), decriminalizing five plant psychedelics and authorizing regulated psilocybin healing centers.

FDA approves Zurzuvae (zuranolone) as the first oral treatment for postpartum depression and issues a CRL for the MDD indication, requiring more studies.
HHS recommends to DEA that marijuana be moved from Schedule I to Schedule III of the Controlled Substances Act.

related_timeline.event: Newsom vetoes SB 58, which would have decriminalized psilocybin and other plant psychedelics, citing the need for dosing and patient-protection guidelines first.

DEA again proposes placing DOI and DOC (phenethylamine research hallucinogens) in Schedule I.

events.asset: Spravato (esketamine nasal spray, Johnson & Johnson): number of patients treated per year
events.entity: Johnson & Johnson (the sponsor that discloses Spravato patient counts)
events.title: Spravato patients treated per year at or above 200,000
events.proposition: The number of patients treated with Spravato (esketamine) in a 12-month period is at or above 200,000, per Johnson & Johnson's public disclosures.
events.criterion: Resolved on the named data series only: Johnson & Johnson's public disclosures (annual report, earnings materials, investor presentations or press releases) of the number of patients treated with Spravato (esketamine) per year or in a stated 12-month period. TRUE on the date of the first such disclosure, dated between the statement date and the window end, that reports 200,000 or more patients treated with Spravato in a 12-month period (worldwide if J&J reports worldwide; US if J&J reports only US). The threshold is in the forecaster's words ('hundreds of thousands', read at its lower bound), so it resolves as binary at 200,000 with no band. FALSE at the window end when no such disclosure reports 200,000 or more. If Johnson & Johnson has published no patient count 12 months after the window end, the event is unresolvable. Realized values are stored, not scored.

resolution_source.name: Johnson & Johnson public disclosures of Spravato patients treated (annual report, earnings materials, investor presentations, press releases)

quantity.metric: Number of patients treated with Spravato (esketamine) in a 12-month period
quantity.series: Johnson & Johnson public disclosures of Spravato patients treated per year

readings: 'Hundreds of thousands' is read at its lower bound, 200,000 patients in a 12-month period (the smallest count that is 'hundreds' of thousands); 'potentially millions' is a hedged higher figure and does not set the threshold.

'This' refers to the '~55k patients ... treated with Spravato per year' figure in the same sentence, so the metric is patients treated per year, on the same series the forecaster cites (J&J's disclosed patient count).
'In a few years' has no N and is not an anchor, so the item is undated (24-month window from the statement date); the forecaster's own horizon is longer than the window, and that is logged.
